questions.stem: Find the area of a rectangle with length 12 m and breadth 8 m.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Area = length × breadth = 12 × 8 = 96 m². Perimeter = 2(12+8) = 40 m. Trap: 80 m² = 10×8 (wrong length); 88 = 11×8; 108 = 12×9.

A triangle has a base of 10 m and a height of 8 m. Find its area.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 10 × 8 = 40 m². Trap: 80 m² forgets the (1/2) factor; 32 uses (1/2)×8×8; 48 uses (1/2)×12×8.

questions.stem: A rectangle (12 m × 8 m) and a square have the same perimeter. By how much does the square's area exceed the rectangle's area?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Perimeter of rectangle = 2(12+8) = 40 m. Square's side = 40/4 = 10 m. Square area = 100 m². Rectangle area = 96 m². Difference = 4 m². Key insight: for the same perimeter, a square always has a greater area than any rectangle — this is a classic SSC concept.

questions.stem: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides of 8 m and 12 m and a height of 6 m.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Area = (1/2) × (sum of parallel sides) × height = (1/2) × (8+12) × 6 = (1/2) × 20 × 6 = 60 m². Trap: 72 = (8+12)/2×(6+1.2) applies wrong height; 80 uses 8×10 (wrong formula); 54 uses (1/2)×(8×12)/2 × 6 (incorrect).

questions.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is 60 m and its length is 18 m. Find its area.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 2(l+b) = 60 → l+b = 30. b = 30−18 = 12 m. Area = 18×12 = 216 m². Trap: 180 = 18×10 (uses b=10, wrong calculation); 240 = 18×(60/4.5) (wrong).

questions.stem: A 2 m wide path runs all around a rectangular garden 50 m long and 30 m wide. Find the area of the path.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Outer dimensions = (50+4) × (30+4) = 54×34 = 1836 m². Inner area = 50×30 = 1500 m². Path area = 1836−1500 = 336 m². Short Trick: area of path = 2×width×(l+b+2×width) = 2×2×(50+30+4) = 4×84 = 336. Trap: 320 = 4×80 (omits the corner adjustment); 400 = 4×(50+30+2×2) = wrong formula.

questions.stem: A ring-shaped region has an outer radius of 7 m and an inner radius of 3.5 m. Find its area. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: C is correct. Area = π(R²−r²) = (22/7)×(7²−3.5²) = (22/7)×(49−12.25) = (22/7)×36.75 = 22×5.25 = 115.5 m². Trap: 96.25 uses only the inner ring area; 121 = π×7² − π×3.5² computed with approximation error.

questions.stem: Find the area of a triangle whose three sides are 13 cm, 14 cm, and 15 cm.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Using Heron's formula: s = (13+14+15)/2 = 21. Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] = √[21×8×7×6] = √7056 = 84 cm². Verify: 21×8=168; 168×7=1176; 1176×6=7056; √7056=84 ✓. This is a 13-14-15 triangle — a classic SSC Heron's formula set. Trap: 78 is the area of a 12-13-14 triangle (similar numbers).
